chift_routes.one_line: Client side: POST /invoices.sales.outstanding.list gives native open amounts (already receivable view) and is joined on AccountHistory.Id with POST /customers.outstanding (or a sideloaded AccountHistory, A) for account number, MatchNo, rate and the partner-line Comment. Supplier side: POST /suppliers.outstanding, with amount/open_amount computed as Credit − Debit (D5) and returned in EUR with rate 1 (D4). Every item takes journal_type from its daybook Type through the shared D6 table (cached POST /daybooks.list) and reference from the D3 header-comment chain; Filter.CompanyIds is omitted to read the whole folder, folder_id follows D7, and Chift emulates pagination.

summary: Horus documents folder-level open-item endpoints for both sides (Guide: Reading accounting data: 'Open items of customers | customers.outstanding', 'Open items of suppliers | suppliers.outstanding'), so no N+1 loop over partners is needed if Filter.CompanyIds is omitted (D: Guide: Making requests: 'omitted or null filters are ignored'; that the result is then complete and uncapped is A). For type=client, POST /invoices.sales.outstanding.list returns document-level open items with a native OpenAmount/OpenCurrencyAmount, a ConfirmedOnly filter, PaymentRemark and Daybook.Id, already in the receivable view (invoice +, payment −). It is joined on AccountHistory.Id with one POST /customers.outstanding call for the account number, MatchNo, rate and partner-line Comment; a sideloaded AccountHistory could replace that call (A). For type=supplier there is no purchase equivalent: POST /suppliers.outstanding returns ledger lines, so amount and open_amount are computed with the shared side-based sign rule (customer Debit − Credit, supplier Credit − Debit, positive = owed; D5). They are returned in EUR with rate 1 because ledger amounts are assumed to be in folder currency (D4, A). Every item takes journal_type from its daybook Type through the shared D6 table (cached POST /daybooks.list). reference is the left part of the header comment, read from the partner-line Comment, then RemarkCompany, then Remark (D3, A), and folder_id follows the single D7 rule. Horus has no paging, so Chift fetches everything, filters on Confirmed, sorts and slices. Main risks: undocumented sign/currency conventions and Partially-matched semantics, item ids that change when the source entry is updated, a single due date with no readable payment method, and an uncertain original_document for carried-forward (IsReport) lines.
verdict_rationale: Horus supports reading open items at folder level for customers and suppliers; the API reference and both the Reading accounting data and Outstanding items & matching guides document it. Under the shared calibration (D11: extra per-request calls, emulated pagination or lost fields mean 'workaround'), Chift's contract still cannot be served 1:1, for four reasons. (1) Each item is assembled from 2-3 endpoints: the open amount; the account number, MatchNo, rate and Comment; and the journal id/type (D6 table). (2) Supplier amount and open_amount are computed from Debit/Credit with the D5 sign rule, because there is no purchase-side OpenAmount. (3) Pagination and total are emulated in Chift. (4) Some fields are lost or approximated. Supplier and client-fallback items of foreign-currency documents are returned in EUR with rate 1 (D4). due_dates has at most one entry and payment_method is not readable. journal_type describes the daybook, not the document (D6). reference relies on an assumed comment location (D3). original_document is uncertain, beneficiaries are outside the endpoints' scope, and item ids are only stable until the source entry is updated. The route is feasible, but it is not a simple transformation, so the verdict is 'workaround' rather than 'supported'.

horus_endpoints.role: type=client primary source. Returns open sale invoices / credit notes and their linked or standalone payments, with native OpenAmount/OpenCurrencyAmount, TotalAmount/TotalCurrencyAmount, DueDate, PaymentRemark, Remark, TransactionType, Daybook.Id, AccountHistory.Id, Company.Id and Confirmed. Its amounts are already in the receivable view (invoice +, payment −; D5). TotalCurrencyAmount/OpenCurrencyAmount are the only invoice-currency amounts available on read (D4). Remark is the last source of the D3 reference chain, and Daybook.Id feeds the D6 journal_type lookup. Filter.ConfirmedOnly implements unposted_allowed=false natively, and Filter.CompanyIds is omitted. Sideloading is supported, so AccountHistory/Daybook could come back in the same call (A: the sideloadable paths are not documented).

horus_endpoints.role: type=client enrichment, joined on AccountHistories[].Id = Data[].AccountHistory.Id. Supplies AccountSearchKey (account_number), MatchDetail.MatchNo (matching_numbers), CurrencyCode/CurrencyRate, IsReport, DocumentNo, Comment (first source of the D3 reference chain) and Confirmed. It also supplies customer lines the sales list does not reference (reconciliation, A), and it is the single-call fallback primary for clients. For those ledger lines, amount = Debit − Credit and open_amount = line or match-group residual Σ(Debit − Credit) (customer side, D5), returned in EUR with rate 1 (D4). The call can be skipped if Horus confirms that AccountHistory can be sideloaded on the sales list with these fields.

call_sequence: 0. [CHIFT_INTERNAL] Resolve consumer_id to the stored Horus connection record: license api_url, access token, single-use refresh token and expiry. Refresh proactively before expiry. FolderId follows the shared D7 rule: folder_id when given. If folder_id is null, use the single folder selected at activation; if no selection is stored, use the single folder returned by POST /folders.list {Mode: 0}; otherwise return Chift 400 'folder_id required'. Send 'Content-Encoding: gzip' on every Horus call below (Guide: Making requests).

1. [both types, cached] POST /daybooks.list {FolderId} -> maps Id -> {SearchKey, Type} and SearchKey -> Id, and Type -> journal_type through the shared D6 table. On a miss, refresh once (daybooks.update can change SearchKey).

2a. [type=client] POST /invoices.sales.outstanding.list {FolderId, Filter:{ConfirmedOnly: (unposted_allowed == 'false')}}, with CompanyIds omitted (not []). Option (A, pending Horus confirmation): add "Include": "AccountHistory,Daybook" and read AccountSearchKey, MatchDetail and CurrencyRate from Included.AccountHistories, which would make step 3a unnecessary.

3a. [type=client] POST /customers.outstanding {FolderId} (Filter omitted, or no CompanyIds) -> index Data.AccountHistories[] by Id (AccountSearchKey, MatchDetail.MatchNo, CurrencyCode, CurrencyRate, IsReport, DocumentNo, Comment, Confirmed, DaybookSearchKey). Run in parallel with 2a.

4a. [type=client] Clean and join. (i) Drop top-level rows whose AccountHistory.Id appears in another row's LinkedElements[] (already netted into that invoice's OpenAmount). (ii) Drop rows with OpenAmount == 0 and log them (?). (iii) Join 2a.Data[].AccountHistory.Id = 3a.AccountHistories[].Id. Rows missing from 3a -> GET /account-histories.info?Id=... (rare N+1). account-histories.info has no Folder field, so the D13 guard runs through the book entry: accept the line only if its Data.BookEntry.Id equals the row's BookEntry.Id, or else GET /book-entries.info on that BookEntry.Id shows Data.Folder.Id = FolderId. A proven mismatch -> Chift 400; an unverifiable line (BookEntry null) -> skip the item and log. (iv) Reconcile (A): emit customers.outstanding lines that no sales-list row references (top-level or LinkedElements) and log them. They use the customer-side ledger rule: amount = Debit − Credit, open_amount = the line's amount or match-group residual Σ(Debit − Credit) (D5), in EUR with rate 1 (D4). Keep AccountType 100, and apply Confirmed==true when unposted_allowed=='false'. (v) Control check (D): compare Σ OpenAmount of the kept sales-list rows (EUR view) plus the reconciliation residuals with SumDebit − SumCredit of 3a (customer-side sign, D5), and log any gap.
2b. [type=supplier] POST /suppliers.outstanding {FolderId} (Filter omitted, or no CompanyIds) -> Data.AccountHistories[].

3b. [type=supplier] Post-filters: keep Confirmed == true when unposted_allowed == 'false'; keep AccountType 200 (defensive, since the docs example is a placeholder); drop MatchDetail.MatchStatus 900 'Totally' (defensive: the guide says outstanding items are lines not matched yet). amount = Credit − Debit (supplier side, D5). A line with MatchNo null gets open_amount = amount. If lines with a non-null MatchNo come back ('0: Partially', A): group by (CompanyDetail.Company.Id, MatchNo), compute residual = Σ(Credit − Debit) (D5), allocate it to the positive (invoice-side) lines oldest DueDate first, and drop fully consumed payment lines.

4b. [type=supplier] journal_id from the daybooks cache (DaybookSearchKey); journal_type from its Type via the shared D6 table. Amounts are returned in EUR with currency 'EUR' and currency_exchange_rate 1, whatever CurrencyCode says (D4, A); a foreign CurrencyCode is logged. Optional payment_communication for lines in a '100: Purchase' or '150: PurchaseCreditNote' daybook: CompanyDetail.RemarkPayment of the line's book entry (A), read in step 4c (GET /book-entries.info per distinct BookEntry.Id by default; POST /book-entries.list per daybook/period as the bulk alternative).

4c. [both, optional enrichment through BookEntry.Id] Collect the distinct BookEntry.Id values of: (i) supplier lines in a purchase daybook (RemarkPayment -> payment_communication, A); (ii) client reconciliation lines from 4a(iv), which have no PaymentRemark (same); (iii) IsReport=true lines on either side (EntryType, Daybook.Id -> original_document, A); (iv) only if the fallback is enabled, invoice-type lines with DueDate null (CompanyDetail.DueDate, A); (v) lines on either side whose partner-line Comment is null or empty (CompanyDetail.RemarkCompany -> reference, second step of the D3 chain, A). Skip Ids already in a cross-request cache keyed by BookEntry.Id (D: an update generates a new book entry, so an invoice update cannot change what a cached Id returned). Call GET /book-entries.info?Id=... for the remaining Ids, with bounded concurrency and the token/500 handling of step 6. A 400/404 (entry replaced since the snapshot) leaves the enrichment null without failing the request. Cross-folder guard (D13): every response must have Data.Folder.Id = FolderId, otherwise return Chift 400. Use an entry's RemarkPayment, RemarkCompany or DueDate only if its CompanyDetail.Company.Id equals the line's partner_id. Cost rule (D): .info costs 1 small call per distinct entry and nothing on a warm cache. POST /book-entries.list {FolderId, DaybookId, Start/End = min/max AccountingMonth/AccountingYear of the group} costs 1 call per daybook but returns every entry of that window, matched or not. Use .list for a daybook group only on a cold cache with many distinct entries and a short window; tune the threshold on a test license, since rate limits are undocumented (A).

5. [both] Map to OutstandingItem. journal_type comes from the daybook Type via the shared D6 table. amount/open_amount use the side-based sign rule (D5). Each item has one currency view: EUR with rate 1 wherever invoice-currency amounts are missing (D4). reference = the first non-empty value of partner-line Comment -> RemarkCompany -> Remark, split on the first ' | ' for invoice-daybook lines (D3). Sort deterministically (date asc, then id asc), set total = item count, return slice [(page-1)*size, page*size). Cache the full result for a short TTL keyed by (consumer, folder, type, unposted_allowed).

6. [errors, Guide: Responses & errors] Horus 401 -> refresh the token once and retry; if it fails again, return a Chift auth error asking the user to reconnect. Horus 400 -> no retry; log Details and return Chift 400 (ChiftError) carrying Horus Details (e.g. unknown FolderId). Horus 403 -> Chift 400 'folder not accessible with this connection' (D7). Horus 404 -> Chift 400 with an explicit error_code (not found), because the Chift contract declares only 400 and 422. A cross-folder mismatch found by the D13 guard -> Chift 400. Horus 500 -> retry with exponential backoff, then a Chift error. An invalid type or unposted_allowed is rejected with Chift 422 before any Horus call.

ALT (only if Horus says folder-level outstanding calls are capped or incomplete). Step 1: POST /fiscal-years.list {IncludeFuture: true}, plus GET /fiscal-years.info per year to read IsClosed (each response checked for Data.Folder.Id = FolderId, D13). Step 2: POST /accounts.list to resolve the concentration accounts (from companies.list) to search keys. Step 3: POST /account-histories.list {FolderId, Start/End, Filter:{NotMatchedOnly: true, ConfirmedOnly: (unposted_allowed=='false'), IncludeCompanyDetail: true, IncludeMatchDetail: true, AccountSearchKeys: [concentration account keys]}}. Keep AccountType 100 or 200, apply the side-based sign rule (D5: Debit − Credit for 100, Credit − Debit for 200) and return amounts in EUR (D4). To avoid double counting, EITHER start at the first year that is not closed and keep IncludeReport at its default (true), OR read the full history with IncludeReport: false (A). Second option: POST /companies.list {IsCustomer|IsSupplier} and batch CompanyIds into customers/suppliers.outstanding.

limitations.description: There is no purchase-side equivalent of invoices.sales.outstanding.list (both guide outstanding tables list only invoices.sales.outstanding.list/.info). Supplier amount and open_amount must be rebuilt from Debit/Credit and MatchDetail with the supplier-side sign rule (Credit − Debit, D5).
limitations.impact: Supplier open amounts are an emulation. If partially matched lines are returned, multi-invoice groups need an allocation rule that may not match Horus's screens. Clients and suppliers are calculated differently.
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: For clients, the sales list lacks account number, MatchNo and currency rate, so it is joined with customers.outstanding on AccountHistory.Id. The two calls are separate snapshots, not one atomic read. Sideloading AccountHistory might remove the second call (A).
limitations.impact: Two calls per request, with possible mismatches if data changes between them (handled by the account-histories.info fallback).
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: Horus has one DueDate per document and no instalment structure; the invoice PaymentMode is write-only.
limitations.impact: due_dates has at most one element. payment_method and payment_method_id are null, or at best filled with the party's usual payment mode.
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: original_document can only be guessed from IsReport lines. IsReport is undefined in the reference and the guides. GET /book-entries.info on the line's BookEntry.Id gives the EntryType of the entry that carries it (e.g. '910: OpeningMO'), which tells whether the line sits in an opening entry, but neither the line nor its book entry links to the prior-year document.
limitations.impact: original_document.id is always null. The other original_document fields are filled, partly filled or null depending on EntryType and on Horus's answer about what report lines keep, at the cost of one cached book-entries.info call per distinct carrier entry.

limitations.description: No documented sign convention: Debit/Credit are number|null and TotalAmount is signed only in an example. The outstanding examples look like placeholders. By general accounting knowledge (not a Horus source), a sale debits the customer account, yet the customers.outstanding example shows a Credit on a 'VEN' line, and the suppliers.outstanding example shows a Debit and AccountType 100 on a '440000 Fournisseurs' / 'ACH' line. The connector applies one side-based rule on every path (D5): customer lines Debit − Credit, supplier lines Credit − Debit, positive = owed; sales-list rows are already in the receivable view.
limitations.impact: The sign of amount/open_amount (especially for suppliers, credit notes and payments) must be validated on a test license or test folder before go-live. Horus has no separate sandbox: 'Requests run against the license's real database.'

limitations.description: Foreign-currency semantics are unclear. Account history lines carry CurrencyCode/CurrencyRate but no foreign-currency amount, and the rate direction is undocumented. Under D4 (A), ledger Debit/Credit are taken as folder-currency (EUR) amounts and are never paired with a foreign currency code.
limitations.impact: Supplier items and client reconciliation/fallback items of foreign-currency documents are returned in EUR, with currency 'EUR' and currency_exchange_rate 1, so the document currency and its amounts are lost for them. Client sales-list rows keep the invoice currency through TotalCurrencyAmount/OpenCurrencyAmount.
limitations.label: A

limitations.description: Beneficiary (employee) open items are not exposed by customers/suppliers.outstanding: AccountType has no beneficiary value, and matching next-number exists only for customer, supplier and account. They can be read as a workaround via account-histories.list {CompanyId, NotMatchedOnly: true} on the beneficiary's current account (BeneficiaryInfo.DefaultCurrentAccount -> account search key).
limitations.impact: Out of scope for this route, since Chift OutstandingType is only client|supplier, even though partner_id mentions employees. A period-bound workaround exists if Chift ever needs it.
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: MatchNo is scoped per company (customer/supplier) or per general account, not per folder.
limitations.impact: matching_numbers values are not unique across partners. Chift consumers must read them with partner_id, which conflicts with Chift MatchingOut's 'Unique number of the matching operation'.
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: Some Horus information has no Chift field: ReminderLevel (customers only), PaymentStatus, LastPaymentDate, LinkedElements detail, VatDetail, and the cash discount (book-entries.list / book-entries.info CompanyDetail.DiscountDetail DiscountDate/DiscountAmount/DiscountRate; written via invoices.*.new Discount).
limitations.impact: Credit-control data such as the reminder level and early-payment discount terms is lost in the unified model.
limitations.label: F

limitations.description: Unconfirmed entries can carry number 0 ('It can be 0 when the invoice is not confirmed'; 'it can be 0 while the entry is not confirmed').
limitations.impact: number is null for unposted items when unposted_allowed=true.
limitations.label: F

limitations.description: Item ids are only as stable as the source entry. Updating an invoice or operation (invoices.*.update, book-entries.*.update) generates a new book entry with a new Id. Its account history lines, and so the Chift outstanding id, presumably change too.
limitations.impact: An outstanding id stored by a Chift consumer can disappear before it is used for matching. Consumers must re-read before matching; fallback business key = journal_id + number + partner_id.
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: Entries pushed through the API, including invoices and payments Chift creates, are unconfirmed by default ('Entries pushed through the API are unconfirmed by default ( Confirmed: false )').
limitations.impact: A consumer that creates an invoice and then reads outstandings with unposted_allowed=false will not see it until the accountant confirms it in Horus Office. Explain this to clients and advise unposted_allowed=true for their own pushed documents (D).
limitations.label: F

limitations.description: The outstanding endpoints cannot be read incrementally. Their Filter has only CompanyIds, IncludeVatDetail and UseAlternateHeading; there is no ModifiedAfter, only a per-line LastModifiedDate.
limitations.impact: Every cache miss reloads the full set. On the ALT path account-histories.list has ModifiedAfter, but a delta cannot reliably remove lines that were replaced (new Ids) or matched, so a full reload stays the v1 rule.
limitations.label: F

limitations.description: customers.outstanding and suppliers.outstanding do not support sideloading (the Sideloading guide lists only book-entries.list, account-histories.list, companies.list and invoices.sales.outstanding.list). Book-entry data such as RemarkPayment, RemarkCompany or EntryType therefore costs separate calls: GET /book-entries.info per distinct BookEntry.Id, or POST /book-entries.list per daybook and period.
limitations.impact: Supplier payment_communication, the RemarkCompany step of the reference chain (D3) and original_document together cost up to one call per distinct book entry on a cold cache. Mitigated by a cross-request cache keyed by BookEntry.Id and by enriching only purchase-daybook, client reconciliation, IsReport and empty-Comment lines. All three Chift fields are optional, so the enrichment can be switched off if latency matters.
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: journal_type is the daybook's type through the shared D6 table, not the document's nature. A credit note posted in a '200: Sale' or '100: Purchase' daybook is reported as customer_invoice / supplier_invoice. The Horus TransactionType of client rows ('1: Sale credit note') has no Chift field.
limitations.impact: Consumers must use the sign of amount/open_amount (D5), not journal_type, to tell credit notes from invoices. In exchange, journal_type stays consistent with Get journals for the same journal_id.
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: reference relies on the D3 header-comment convention and on an assumed read location (partner-line Comment → RemarkCompany → Remark), none of which Horus documents as the invoice header Comment.
limitations.impact: reference may be null or come from the wrong field until Horus confirms. Comments typed outside Chift that contain ' | ' are cut to their left part. customer_memo has no OutstandingItem field and is dropped.
limitations.label: A

edge_cases.case: A payment linked to an invoice is returned twice by invoices.sales.outstanding.list: inside the invoice's LinkedElements[] and as its own top-level row with OpenAmount null. The duplication itself is F (raw example: payment 220065 with AccountHistory.Id 'eidhge75-...').
edge_cases.handling: Drop top-level rows whose AccountHistory.Id appears in any LinkedElements[], because the invoice's OpenAmount already nets them (1210 - 210 = 1000 in the example).
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Unallocated customer payment or credit balance (top-level row with TransactionType '2: Payment' not linked to any invoice).
edge_cases.handling: Return it as an item with journal_type from its daybook (D6, typically financial_operation for '500: Bank'), a negative amount (receivable view, D5) and open_amount = TotalAmount (OpenAmount is null for payments). Ask Chift whether credit balances should be included.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Sale credit note (TransactionType '1: Sale credit note'), or a credit note booked in an invoice daybook (invoices.*.new Type 1 with a 100/200 daybook).
edge_cases.handling: journal_type follows the daybook through the D6 table. A credit note in a '250: SaleCreditNote' / '150: PurchaseCreditNote' daybook gets customer_refund / supplier_refund; one posted in a '200: Sale' / '100: Purchase' daybook keeps customer_invoice / supplier_invoice, because journal_type describes the daybook (D1/D6). Its nature shows through the sign: negative amount and open_amount under D5. Sales-list rows are already negative in the receivable view; on ledger lines it is a net credit on a customer line or a net debit on a supplier line. Whether a Type 1 document can sit in a 200/100 daybook is the D1 open question.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Partially matched group with several invoices and payments (MatchStatus '0: Partially', same MatchNo), if customers/suppliers.outstanding return such lines.
edge_cases.handling: Compute the residual per (Company.Id, MatchNo) with the side-based formula (D5: Σ(Debit − Credit) for customer lines, Σ(Credit − Debit) for supplier lines). Allocate it to the positive (invoice-side) lines oldest DueDate first, drop the payment lines, and put MatchNo in matching_numbers of the remaining lines. If Horus confirms that only unmatched lines are returned, this branch never runs.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: MatchDetail with MatchStatus 0 but MatchNo null (both the customers.outstanding and the suppliers.outstanding examples show this).
edge_cases.handling: Treat as unmatched: open_amount = amount, matching_numbers = []. Status 0 may simply be the default for unmatched lines (A).

edge_cases.case: Unconfirmed (draft) entry with number 0, requested with unposted_allowed=false.
edge_cases.handling: Excluded natively (ConfirmedOnly=true) or by the post-filter Confirmed==true. With unposted_allowed=true: posted=false, number=null.
edge_cases.label: F

edge_cases.case: Invoice pushed through Chift (Confirmed false by default) read back immediately.
edge_cases.handling: With unposted_allowed=true it appears with posted=false and possibly number null (Number 0). With false it is absent until the accountant confirms it.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Line carried forward from a previous fiscal year (IsReport=true).
edge_cases.handling: Read the EntryType of its book entry with GET /book-entries.info (cached). '100: Normal' in a sale or purchase daybook: fill original_document from the line's own fields (A). '910: OpeningMO' or another closing/opening MO: number, journal_id and journal_type null; date/due_date/reference only if Horus confirms report lines keep them. BookEntry null, or Horus says report lines keep no original data: null.

edge_cases.case: Foreign-currency invoice (CurrencyCode or Currency e.g. 'USD').
edge_cases.handling: Client sales-list row: TotalCurrencyAmount/OpenCurrencyAmount with currency = Currency and CurrencyRate from the joined line. If an invoice-currency amount is missing, return the EUR amounts with currency 'EUR' and rate 1 (D4). Supplier line, or client reconciliation/fallback line: amounts in EUR, currency 'EUR', rate 1 (D4). Log the CurrencyCode and disclose the loss as a limitation. Never return EUR amounts under 'USD'.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Line with CompanyDetail null or Company null (e.g. a misc operation on the collective account without a counterparty).
edge_cases.handling: partner_id is required, so skip the item and log a warning.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Partner that is both customer and supplier (IsCustomer and IsSupplier both true).
edge_cases.handling: It appears in both lists with different accounts (AccountType 100 vs 200). There is no netting between them, which matches Chift's type split.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Partner that is a beneficiary (BeneficiaryType '10: Employee').
edge_cases.handling: Returned by neither type value. Their open lines are readable only via account-histories.list {CompanyId, NotMatchedOnly: true} on the beneficiary current account; out of scope and documented as a limitation.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: DaybookSearchKey (or a client row's Daybook.Id) not found in the cached daybooks.list (renamed via daybooks.update, or a new daybook).
edge_cases.handling: Refresh the cache once. If it is still missing, set journal_type 'unknown' (D6) and log it. journal_id is required: client rows still have Daybook.Id; for ledger lines, return the search key only as a last resort.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Sales-list row whose AccountHistory.Id is missing from the customers.outstanding snapshot.
edge_cases.handling: GET /account-histories.info?Id=... to fill account_number, MatchNo, CurrencyRate and Comment. D13 guard through the book entry, because the response has no Folder field: accept the line if its BookEntry.Id equals the row's BookEntry.Id, or else if book-entries.info on that BookEntry.Id shows Data.Folder.Id = FolderId. A proven mismatch -> Chift 400; an unverifiable line (BookEntry null) -> skip the item and log.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: customers.outstanding line that no sales-list row references, top-level or in LinkedElements (e.g. a carried-forward or opening line).
edge_cases.handling: Emit it with the customer-side ledger rule and log it, until Horus confirms whether the sales list is complete. The rule: amount = Debit − Credit; open_amount from the line and its match group with Σ(Debit − Credit) (D5); EUR with rate 1 (D4); journal_type from the daybook via D6.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Outstanding id no longer exists at matching time, because the invoice or operation was updated (invoices.*.update / book-entries.*.update generate a new book entry).
edge_cases.handling: Do not cache item ids beyond the short pagination TTL. Chift consumers re-read outstandings before matching. Map the Horus 400/404 from POST /matching to a clear 'stale item' Chift error, and reconcile on journal_id + number + partner_id, as the guide recommends.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Sales-list row with PaymentStatus '800: Paid' or OpenAmount == 0 on an 'open invoices' endpoint.
edge_cases.handling: Exclude it when OpenAmount == 0, which is not outstanding and not counted in total. PaymentStatus alone is not trusted, because the example shows '10' with LastPaymentDate null. Ask Horus whether such rows can occur.

edge_cases.case: Line created with a pre-assigned MatchNo (invoices / operation lines accept MatchNo at creation together with matching.next-number.*) whose counterpart does not exist yet, or is unconfirmed and filtered out.
edge_cases.handling: If Horus returns it: a single-line group gives open_amount = amount and matching_numbers = [MatchNo]. When unposted_allowed=false filters out an unconfirmed counterpart, compute the residual only on the lines kept and document this. Whether Horus treats such a line as 'matched' and hides it from outstanding is undocumented.

edge_cases.case: Unknown or inaccessible FolderId, or folder_id missing while the connection has several selected folders.
edge_cases.handling: Shared D7 rule. folder_id missing with several selected folders -> Chift 400 'folder_id required' before any Horus call. Horus 403 -> Chift 400 'folder not accessible with this connection'. Horus 400/404 -> Chift 400 (ChiftError) with Horus Details and an explicit error_code. No retry.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Access token expires during the fetch (tokens last 1 hour).
edge_cases.handling: Refresh once and retry the failed call (refresh tokens are single-use, so persist the new one before retrying). If the refresh fails, mark the connection disconnected and ask the user to reconnect.
edge_cases.label: F

edge_cases.case: Empty folder, or a folder with no open items.
edge_cases.handling: Return items=[] and total=0.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Very large folder (thousands of open lines).
edge_cases.handling: Full fetch per cache miss with gzip (the guide prescribes a 'Content-Encoding: gzip' request header; general HTTP practice would use Accept-Encoding, so test that the documented header works). Serve pages from a short TTL cache keyed by (consumer, folder, type, unposted_allowed). Rate limits and timeouts are undocumented.

edge_cases.case: Outstanding line whose BookEntry is null.
edge_cases.handling: No book-entry enrichment. payment_communication comes from Memo (bank/financial lines) or is null; reference skips the RemarkCompany step of the D3 chain; original_document is null.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: GET /book-entries.info returns 400/404 for a BookEntry.Id read moments earlier from the outstanding list (the invoice or operation was updated in between, which generates a new book entry).
edge_cases.handling: Leave that item's enrichment (payment_communication, the RemarkCompany step of reference, original_document) null or fall through to the next source, log it, and neither fail the page nor retry. The next cache miss reloads the outstanding set with the new line and entry Ids. Which status Horus returns for a replaced entry is undocumented.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: One book entry carries several open lines: an opening entry for many partners, or a bank statement paying several suppliers.
edge_cases.handling: Call book-entries.info once per distinct BookEntry.Id and reuse the result for all its lines. CompanyDetail is a single object per entry, so apply RemarkPayment, RemarkCompany or DueDate only when CompanyDetail.Company.Id equals the line's partner_id; otherwise use Memo (bank lines), the next source of the D3 chain, or null.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Invoice or credit-note line (purchase or sale daybook) whose own DueDate is null.
edge_cases.handling: Return due_date null and due_dates []. If Horus confirms that book-entries.info CompanyDetail.DueDate holds the invoice due date, enable the optional fallback of step 4c(iv).
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Header comment on an invoice-daybook line that contains ' | ' but was not written by Chift (e.g. typed by the accountant in Horus Office), or that starts with '| ' (customer_memo only).
edge_cases.handling: Apply the D3 split anyway: the left part becomes reference, so a native comment containing ' | ' is truncated; a leading '| ' gives reference null. Log the split. Lines outside invoice daybooks (payments, misc operations) are not split.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: An Id-only call (GET /book-entries.info, or GET /fiscal-years.info on the ALT path) returns Data.Folder.Id different from FolderId.
edge_cases.handling: D13 cross-folder guard: do not use the data, log it, and return Chift 400. The Id came from a FolderId-scoped response, so a mismatch signals a data integrity problem rather than a user error.
edge_cases.label: D

open_questions.question: If Filter.CompanyIds is omitted, do customers.outstanding, suppliers.outstanding and invoices.sales.outstanding.list return the open lines of every customer/supplier in the folder? Is there a size cap or hidden pagination, and what does an explicit empty array [] do?
open_questions.why: Decides between 1 folder-level call and per-company batching. The Making requests guide says 'omitted or null filters are ignored', but the PAGE TEXT and the matching guide say 'a customer's' (singular), while the Reading accounting data guide says 'Open items of customers'.

open_questions.question: Do customers/suppliers.outstanding return lines with MatchStatus '0: Partially', and if so every line of the partial group, including payments? Does account-histories.list NotMatchedOnly also exclude partially matched lines?
open_questions.why: The guide defines outstanding items as 'lines that are not matched yet' but does not define Partially. This decides whether supplier open_amount needs group netting.

open_questions.question: What is the sign convention of Debit/Credit on outstanding lines? The connector assumes (D5) that Debit − Credit on customer lines (AccountType 100) and Credit − Debit on supplier lines (AccountType 200) give the amount owed. Is that correct?
open_questions.why: The examples look like placeholders (Credit on a VEN customer line; Debit and AccountType 100 on a 440000 supplier line), and amount/open_amount depend on the answer.

open_questions.question: Direction and meaning of CurrencyRate; currency of CompanyDetail amounts. Are account-history Debit/Credit and book-entry CompanyDetail amounts always in the folder currency (EUR)? Is CurrencyRate EUR per unit of CurrencyCode, or units per EUR?
open_questions.why: Until this is confirmed, D4 returns ledger-line amounts of foreign-currency documents in EUR with currency 'EUR' and rate 1. A confirmed rule could restore the document currency for supplier items.

open_questions.question: What does IsReport mean exactly? Does an IsReport=true line keep the original DocumentNo, Date, DueDate and Daybook, which EntryType does its book entry have (e.g. '910: OpeningMO'), and is there any link to the prior-year account history?
open_questions.why: Decides whether original_document can be filled or must be null. book-entries.info gives the carrier entry's EntryType, but not what the line keeps.

open_questions.question: Does invoices.sales.outstanding.list include invoices carried forward from previous fiscal years and every customer line that customers.outstanding returns? Why is a linked payment also returned as a top-level row, and can rows with PaymentStatus '800: Paid' or OpenAmount 0 occur?
open_questions.why: Completeness, deduplication and the reconciliation step for client items.

open_questions.question: What does MatchStatus 0 ('Partially') mean when MatchNo is null?
open_questions.why: Both outstanding examples show this combination, and it affects open_amount and matching_numbers.

open_questions.question: On invoices.sales.outstanding.list, can Include contain 'AccountHistory' and 'Daybook'? Do Included.AccountHistories carry AccountSearchKey, MatchDetail and CurrencyRate, and Included.Daybooks carry Type? On account-histories.list, can Include 'BookEntry' return CompanyDetail.RemarkPayment?
open_questions.why: The Sideloading guide documents the syntax and the supported endpoints but not the paths or fields. A yes would reduce the client side to one call and, on the ALT path, deliver RemarkPayment without per-entry book-entries.info calls (customers/suppliers.outstanding are not sideloadable, so the main path needs book-entries.info or book-entries.list).

open_questions.question: On book-entries.info / book-entries.list, does CompanyDetail.RemarkPayment contain the PaymentReferences written through invoices.*.new, CompanyDetail.DueDate the invoice DueDate, and RemarkCompany the invoice-level Comment?
open_questions.why: These CompanyDetail fields have no description (the book-entries.info example shows them all null). RemarkPayment is the only candidate for supplier payment_communication, DueDate would serve as a due_date fallback, and RemarkCompany is the second source of the D3 reference chain.

open_questions.question: Where does the invoice header Comment surface on read (partner-line Comment, RemarkCompany, Remark)?
open_questions.why: reference is read through the D3 chain: partner-line Comment, then RemarkCompany, then Remark. The RemarkCompany step costs a book-entries.info call per entry, and none of the three fields is documented as the header Comment.

open_questions.question: Can a credit note (Type 1) be posted into a 200/100 daybook, and an invoice into 250/150?
open_questions.why: journal_type describes the daybook (D6). If credit notes can sit in invoice daybooks, consumers must rely on the sign (D5) to identify them, and the shared D1 rule depends on the same answer.

open_questions.question: Can book-entries.info take several Ids in one call, or can sideloading of BookEntry be enabled on customers/suppliers.outstanding (the Sideloading guide invites requests for other endpoints)? Which status does book-entries.info return for an entry replaced by an update?
open_questions.why: Supplier enrichment otherwise costs one call per distinct book entry on a cold cache, and the 400/404 handling of replaced entries depends on the answer.

open_questions.question: Can GET /account-histories.info return the line's Folder reference, as book-entries.info and fiscal-years.info do?
open_questions.why: Its response has no Folder field, so the D13 cross-folder guard must go through the line's BookEntry, which can cost an extra book-entries.info call. Low priority (rare fallback path).

open_questions.question: Does a line created with a pre-assigned MatchNo, with no counterpart yet, still appear in customers/suppliers.outstanding?
open_questions.why: If it counts as matched, open invoices created that way would silently disappear from the outstanding list.

open_questions.question: When an invoice/operation is updated and a new book entry is generated, do its account history lines get new Ids? Does POST /matching keep line Ids unchanged?
open_questions.why: The Chift outstanding id is the account history Id, so its stability matters for matching.

open_questions.question: Is there, or will there be, a purchase-side open-invoice endpoint with OpenAmount?
open_questions.why: It would remove the supplier open-amount emulation.

open_questions.question: For invoices.sales.outstanding.info, is the 'Id' query parameter the FolderId the guide mentions?
open_questions.why: The guide says it 'requires the FolderId', but the schema has no parameter with that name. Low priority (not used in the list flow).

open_questions.question: What rate limits, request timeouts and maximum response sizes apply? Is 'Content-Encoding: gzip' on the request really what triggers gzipped responses?
open_questions.why: The route fetches the full open-item set on every cache miss.

open_questions.question: What sign convention is expected for amount/open_amount (credit notes, payments, supplier invoices)? The connector proposes D5: positive = owed (receivable for clients, payable for suppliers), with credit notes and payments negative.
open_questions.why: The contract only says 'Total amount' and 'Open amount'.

open_questions.question: Should unallocated payments and credit balances be returned as outstanding items?
open_questions.why: Horus returns them (TransactionType 2 rows), and they affect totals.

open_questions.question: Is due_dates[].amount the scheduled amount or the remaining amount per due date? The connector returns the item currency only where Horus gives invoice-currency amounts (client sales-list rows) and EUR with rate 1 otherwise (D4): is that acceptable? Is the party's usual payment mode acceptable as a payment_method fallback?
open_questions.why: Horus gives a single due date, both EUR and currency amounts on the client side only, and no invoice-level payment method on read.

open_questions.question: Is a partner-scoped matching number acceptable in matching_numbers, or should the connector prefix it (e.g. with the partner)?
open_questions.why: Horus MatchNo is unique per company/account only, while Chift MatchingOut describes matching_number as 'Unique'.

open_questions.question: Will consumers pass outstanding item ids (Horus account history lines) to POST /accounting/matching, or invoice/journal entry ids?
open_questions.why: MatchingIn.entries says entries are 'typically journal entry id, invoice id or financial entry id', while Horus matching takes account history line ids. The matching connector must resolve book entry ids to partner lines if consumers send entry ids.

open_questions.question: Should employee items be returned under type=supplier for connectors where that is possible?
open_questions.why: OutstandingType has only client/supplier, while partner_id mentions employees.

evidence_gaps: Pagination: D, not F. The Making requests and Responses & errors guides define the request/response envelope (Filter object, Data object or array, Included for sideloads, error object) and mention no paging, size cap or total. Rate limits and timeouts remain ? (not in any provided page; Support & FAQ not provided).

Sideloading: the guide documents the syntax (Include with comma-separated dot paths, Included indexed by Type) and the 4 supported endpoints (book-entries.list, account-histories.list, companies.list, invoices.sales.outstanding.list). It does not say which relationship paths each endpoint can sideload, or which fields a sideloaded entity carries (the example returns a reduced Companies object).

Definitions: the Data model and Outstanding items & matching guides define folder, company, daybook, book entry, account history line, Confirmed and outstanding items ('Lines that are not matched yet'). Still undefined: IsReport, MatchStatus '0: Partially', and whether partially matched lines count as outstanding.

No documented sign convention for Debit/Credit or TotalAmount; the side-based rule (D5) is applied as an assumption. The outstanding examples are placeholders (Credit on a VEN customer line; Debit and AccountType 100 on a 440000 supplier line; VatDetail filled although IncludeVatDetail is false).

The behaviour of an explicit empty CompanyIds array is undocumented, yet the raw request examples send "CompanyIds": [] (horus.md l.19390, 19962, 24410). The omitted/null rule comes from the generic Filter rule in Making requests, which is worded for 'Most .list endpoints'.
Whether account history line Ids change when their book entry is updated is not stated. Only the book entry is documented: 'generates a new book entry'.

book-entries.list / book-entries.info CompanyDetail.RemarkPayment (like RemarkCompany, DueDate, PaymentDate and TotalAmount) has no description; the link of RemarkPayment to the PaymentReferences write field is assumed.
The ExcludedEntryTypes / EntryTypes enum on account-histories.list has no labels there; labels come from book-entries.list / book-entries.info EntryType.
invoices.sales.outstanding.info: the guide says it 'requires the FolderId', but the schema exposes only 'Id' (+ BookEntryId / BookEntryNumber).

book-entries.info is documented: its page was supplied separately and is rendered in the reference ('Get details for a specific book entry.', param Id *), consistent with Guide: Reading accounting data ('Use book-entries.info to get the full detail of one entry'). Remaining gaps: its CompanyDetail fields have no descriptions and the example shows them all null; no FolderId parameter, batch form or sideloading is documented for it; the status returned for an entry replaced by an update is not stated.

The Quickstart, Support & FAQ, Changelog, Postman collection and tax-combination spreadsheets were not provided. This route does not depend on them, except the Changelog for any future paging/limit parameter.

ba_insights: Terminology comes first (F, Guide: Data model). Horus folder = 'the accounting record of one company' = Chift folder. Horus company = a counterparty of the folder ('the legal entities a folder deals with: customers, suppliers and beneficiaries') = Chift partner, not the folder's own entity. Daybook = journal, identified by a SearchKey such as ACH/VEN. Book entry = the journal entry. Account history line = 'one line per account movement, with debit/credit amounts, VAT information, matching number'. MatchNo = matching (lettering) number, scoped per company.

Is it N+1? No. customers.outstanding, suppliers.outstanding and invoices.sales.outstanding.list all take a FolderId plus an optional CompanyIds filter. Omitting the filter is the documented way to apply no filter (D: 'omitted or null filters are ignored'). The single assumption to confirm with Horus is that the result is then complete and uncapped (A). Do not send [], whose behaviour is undocumented.

Why several calls (the case's hint): no single Horus endpoint holds a full Chift OutstandingItem. For clients, the open amount comes from the sales open-items list, account_number/MatchNo/rate/Comment from customers.outstanding, and journal_type from daybooks through the shared D6 table. For suppliers, open_amount does not exist in Horus and is calculated (D5).

The route is asymmetric. Clients get a native OpenAmount, PaymentRemark and ConfirmedOnly filter; suppliers get only ledger lines. Tell the client that the two lists are built differently and that supplier figures are a reconstruction, though a simple one if Horus confirms that only unmatched lines are returned.

Id choice: use the account history line Id. The guide makes it the unit of matching ('Call matching with both line Ids'), and a BookEntry.Id is not unique per item (one bank statement entry can pay several partners). It is valid only until the entry is updated, because an update generates a new book entry, so consumers must re-read before matching. Chift's MatchingIn describes entries as 'typically journal entry id, invoice id or financial entry id', so the matching connector should accept both forms.

unposted_allowed maps to Horus 'Confirmed' (validated by the accountant): a native ConfirmedOnly filter on the sales list and a post-filter elsewhere. Entries pushed through the API are unconfirmed by default, so a client who pushes invoices via Chift and reads with unposted_allowed=false will not see them until the accountant confirms them.

Pagination is entirely Chift's job: fetch everything, sort deterministically, slice and count. Use gzip and a short cache. There is no incremental read on the outstanding endpoints, so every cache miss reloads. Deserialise leniently (Guide: Changes & versioning: 'Ignore unknown properties'), so that a future optional paging parameter or new property does not break the connector.

Do not trust the Horus examples for signs. By general accounting knowledge, a sale debits the customer account, yet the customer example shows a Credit on a VEN line and the supplier example shows a Debit and AccountType 100 on a 440000 line. The connector therefore applies one side-based rule on every path (D5): customer lines Debit − Credit, supplier lines Credit − Debit. Positive always means 'owed', which matches the sales list's receivable view (invoice +, payment −). Validate it on a test license or test folder; Horus has no separate sandbox, and requests hit the license's real database.
Dedup trap: a payment linked to an invoice appears both inside the invoice (LinkedElements) and as its own row. Emitting both would double-count it.

Fields that are lost or approximated, to state upfront: due_dates has at most 1 entry (one due date in Horus); payment_method is null (write-only in Horus); original_document is uncertain (IsReport undefined); supplier and client-fallback items of foreign-currency documents come back in EUR with rate 1 (D4); journal_type describes the daybook rather than the document (D6); reference depends on an assumed comment location (D3); cash-discount terms and the reminder level are dropped; and beneficiary open items are out of scope.

Optimisation path to present as conditional: sideloading (Include 'AccountHistory,Daybook') on invoices.sales.outstanding.list could make the client side a single call. Syntax and endpoint support are documented, but the sideloadable paths are not, so it is A until Horus confirms.

Label convention used in this mapping: each row carries the weakest label among its branches (e.g. journal_id is F on the client side but D on the supplier side, so the row is D), and stronger sub-labels are stated inline in the rule.

journal_type is the journal's type, as Chift defines it ('the type of journal in which the outstanding item is recorded'). It therefore comes from the daybook Type through the one table shared by all routes (D6), which keeps an item's journal_type identical to what Get journals returns for the same journal_id. A credit note posted in a sales daybook reads customer_invoice; explain to clients that the negative amount (D5), not journal_type, identifies it.

Currency rule (D4): never pair EUR amounts with a foreign currency code. Horus gives invoice-currency amounts only on the sales open-items list (TotalCurrencyAmount/OpenCurrencyAmount). Ledger lines carry a CurrencyCode and CurrencyRate but, by assumption, EUR amounts. So the supplier item of a USD invoice is returned as EUR with rate 1 and flagged, rather than as USD figures that are really EUR.

reference follows the shared header-comment convention (D3). create_invoice writes '{reference} | {customer_memo}' into the Horus Comment. This route reads it back from the partner-line Comment, then RemarkCompany, then the sales-list Remark, and keeps only the left part (OutstandingItem has no customer_memo). The read location is an assumption until Horus answers.

folder_id follows one rule across all routes (D7): required when the connection has more than one selected folder, otherwise the single selected or single accessible folder. A Horus 403 becomes Chift 400 'folder not accessible with this connection'. Id-only calls (book-entries.info, fiscal-years.info) are checked against the folder (D13).
